tytul: Cucumber pickles in oil with garlic: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for canned cucumber pickles in a vinegar brine with oil and raw garlic.

ostrzezenia.tekst: NCHFP research found that garlic-in-oil mixtures stored at room temperature are at risk of botulism.
There are no validated processes for vegetables and herbs in oil made at home; in the USA, the rules for such products apply only to commercial processors.

akapity: The USDA Complete Guide has only 3 tested procedures for vegetables with oil: marinated peppers, marinated whole mushrooms and marinated three-bean salad, and all of them use acid.
None of them is a cucumber pickle.
Acidifying whole garlic cloves in vinegar is a lengthy and highly variable process, so there are no guidelines for acidifying whole garlic cloves at home.
The whole product needs a minimum, uniform level of acid to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity; use only recipes with tested proportions.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for cucumber pickles with oil and raw garlic from a checked source.
JarAtlas has cards for tested cucumber pickle recipes without oil, such as fresh-pack dill pickles and bread and butter pickles.
